subject: Re: Follow-up: Rerank model validation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T15:02:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Rerank model validation & next steps

Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of discovery:
- You prioritize precision at top-k (NDCG@10) and better relevance for low-frequency queries.
- Current production pipeline uses a pointwise scoring model; you want to evaluate a dedicated neural reranker.
- Constraints: latency target <= 120ms P95 for single-request rerank, budget guidance around reserved capacity (monthly commit) once we show unit cost improvements.

What we recommend to validate fit:
1) Models to evaluate (shortlist):
   - rerank-3b-v1 (baseline neural reranker; quantized for throughput)
   - rerank-1.4b-ltr (lighter-weight, good for strict latency)
   - fallback: classic-ensemble (current prod) for A/B baseline
2) Benchmark artifacts we'll share: held-out test set (10k queries), prompt-sets.csv (example prompts/labels), and the benchmark report (NDCG/MRR tables). Links/attachments below.
3) Validation plan:
   - Offline eval: run NDCG@1/5/10, MRR, and error analysis on the 10k set.
   - Online A/B: 2-week 50/50 experiment on a representative query slice (~10% traffic initially), primary metric NDCG@10 + business metric (CTR).
   - Guardrails: automatic rollback if NDCG@10 drops >1.5% or latency P95 exceeds 120ms.

Next steps/action items:
- We (Redwood) will send the benchmark report, prompt sets, and a short model recommendation note (attached). Marcus will run the validation and share initial NDCG/MRR numbers by Friday.
- Alex/Penny: confirm access to the sample production logs we discussed so Marcus can reproduce offline ranking order.

Attachments: acme_rerank-benchmark-report.pdf (summary + tables), acme_prompt-sets.csv (gold labels + prompts)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up if you want Marcus and I to walk through the report live.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before Marcus runs the offline tests: 

1) For the 10k held-out set, can you confirm how labels were generated (human annotation vs. click labels)? We care about label noise.
2) For the latency guardrail, does the 120ms P95 assume 8-token rerank or variable-length inputs? Our average context is ~60 tokens.

If you can answer those two, we'll unblock access to the logs this afternoon. Also please include the raw NDCG/MRR tables in the PDF (we need to present to our search lead).

—Alex
Alex Johnson

Acme Corp

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T17:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Rerank model validation & next steps

Alex — thanks, quick answers and I attached the raw tables in the PDF for the reviewers. Notes from the offline validation run I completed this afternoon against your 10k held-out: 

Methodology recap:
- Label source: hybrid — 70% human-annotated relevance judgments, 30% high-signal click-derived labels (we flagged click-label noise and weighted accordingly during evaluation).
- Tokenization/length: we evaluated on actual query+doc lengths (~median 58 tokens, 90th pct 94 tokens). Latency numbers use your average context distribution.

Key offline results (baseline = classic-ensemble):
- rerank-3b-v1 (quantized): NDCG@10 = 0.520 (baseline 0.420) => +23.8% relative
- rerank-1.4b-ltr: NDCG@10 = 0.498 => +18.6% relative
- MRR: baseline 0.310 -> rerank-3b-v1 0.390 (+25.8%), rerank-1.4b-ltr 0.372 (+20.0%)
- Latency P95 (prod-simulated): rerank-3b-v1 (quant) = 110ms, rerank-1.4b-ltr = 82ms, classic-ensemble = 65ms
- Token cost estimates (per-request): rerank-3b-v1 ~1.7x cost vs baseline, rerank-1.4b-ltr ~1.2x (we provide batching and KV-cache suggestions to narrow this gap)

A/B plan suggestion:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): 50/50 traffic split, primary metric NDCG@10, secondary CTR and conversion. Target statistical significance for NDCG@10 with the 10% traffic slice; we'll calculate required sample sizes if you prefer a different traffic allocation.
- Monitoring: daily NDCG delta, latency P95, error rates; automatic fallback to baseline if guardrail thresholds breach.
- Rollout path: start with rerank-1.4b-ltr for lower-cost proof, then promote rerank-3b-v1 if we need incremental gains and latency/cost are acceptable.

Deliverables I uploaded: acme_rerank-benchmark-report.pdf (full tables + per-query slices), acme_prompt-sets.csv (sample prompt + labels). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-rerank-benchmarks

Let me know if you want the per-query breakdown for top error buckets (we flagged ~120 queries where relevance labels disagree across annotators — likely long-tail knowledge queries). Happy to set up a 30-minute walkthrough with Marissa and me.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Thanks — Alex
